n: Maritime Evasion: Flag Hopping, AIS Manipulation and Ship-to-Ship Transfers
ds: Vessels linked to proliferation-sensitive trade may change flags, ownership and names, disable or falsify identification signals, and conduct cargo transfers at sea. Maritime due diligence uses vessel history, tracking data and ownership analysis to identify these behaviours without relying only on documents.

src.t: FATF, Guidance on Counter Proliferation Financing (2018)
US Department of State, Department of the Treasury (OFAC) and US Coast Guard, Guidance to Address Illicit Shipping and Sanctions Evasion Practices (2020)
UN Security Council 1718 Committee Panel of Experts, Final Report (specify year; mandate ended April 2024)

rat: Shipowners, managers and charterers using flag hopping, AIS manipulation and STS transfers; vessel is the real asset; insurance and P&I changes.

ind.cx: Vessel stops transmitting position data for extended periods near ports or transhipment areas of concern.
ind.fp: Poor coverage and equipment faults cause gaps.
ind.ds: Vessel stops transmitting position data for extended periods near ports or transhipment areas of concern.

ind.n: Frequent flag changes or flagging in registries with weak oversight
ind.cx: Short intervals between flag changes or use of open registries with poor enforcement.
ind.fp: Sale and commercial reasons motivate flag changes.
ind.ds: Short intervals between flag changes or use of open registries with poor enforcement.

ind.cx: Vessel meets others at sea away from regular transfer zones, followed by changed destination.
ind.fp: STS operations are routine in certain trades.
ind.ds: Vessel meets others at sea off normal transfer areas, followed by a changed declared destination.
ind.cn: Ship-to-ship transfers without clear commercial purpose

ind.n: Ownership and management by shell entities with rapid changes
ind.cx: Vessel owner or manager changes frequently, with newly formed companies and shared addresses.
ind.fp: Single-ship companies are normal in shipping.
ind.ds: Entities are repeatedly formed, abandoned or replaced by successors sharing directors, addresses or history of prior defaulted companies.
ind.cn: Short-lived or rotating entities with common controllers

ind.cx: Physical details, IMO or name do not match registry records, or signs of identity spoofing.
ind.ds: Physical details, IMO or name do not match registry records, or signs of identity spoofing.

ind.n: Port calls at locations of concern followed by false next port
ind.cx: Vessel declares destinations inconsistent with subsequent movements.
ind.ds: Vessel declares destinations inconsistent with subsequent movements.

ind.n: Payments for bunkers, port fees or crew from unrelated parties
ind.cx: Operating costs paid by third parties unconnected to the shipowner or charterer.
ind.fp: Ship agents pay on behalf of owners.
ind.ds: Payments are made by parties with no apparent link to the underlying transaction, goods or services.
ind.cn: Payments from or for third parties unrelated to the underlying trade

ind.n: Insurance, classification or P&I cover absent or changed abruptly
ind.cx: Cover is cancelled, provided by unknown insurers or classification society changes.
ind.ds: Cover is cancelled, provided by unknown insurers or classification society changes.

ctl.ds: Compares shipping routes, ports and delivery points with typical lanes and risk lists, and requests explanation for unusual hubs or indirect delivery. It reveals diversion, transshipment and evasion routing.

Uses satellite imagery, land-cover and site evidence to test claims about operations, land use, production or activity at a location. It provides independent physical verification that does not rely on counterparty documents.

ctl.n: Vessel due diligence and tracking analytics
ctl.ds: Verifies vessel identity, ownership, flag history, insurance and class, and analyses tracking data for gaps, loitering, ship-to-ship transfers and spoofing. It addresses sanctions and illicit-trade evasion at sea.

ctl.n: Country, corridor and port risk rating framework
ctl.ds: Maintains documented risk ratings of countries, corridors, ports and booking centres drawn from transparency, corruption and mutual-evaluation sources, updated on a schedule and after relevant events. The ratings feed due diligence, monitoring and limits.

Requires documentary evidence of origin, legal sourcing, custody and conformity with responsible-sourcing standards, including for informal or recycled supply. It keeps illicitly sourced goods from entering the financed or traded chain.

Routes potential sanctions, proscription or restricted-party exposure to a specialist sanctions or legal team for decision before proceeding, and sets conditions for finance and insurance. It ensures complex legal judgements are made by qualified people.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

Cross-checks asset ownership, title history, security registrations and registry changes against official registers, including for changes close to designation or transaction dates. It confirms that the person presenting an asset genuinely owns it.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.
